titulo: Light model for routine work, top model for the hard stuff
lead: You don't call your most experienced business partner to copy a spreadsheet. Models work the same way: the light model is fast and uses less of your plan, and it handles routine work; the top model thinks more slowly and is for the big plan, the hard problem, and anything that could cost a lot. The routing rule spells this out once.
objetivo: write the rule that decides which model handles each task and classify your tasks as light or top.

aprende.t: Which model is light and which is top in your tools
When to move up to the top model, and explain why
Choose the model in chat and in the terminal

hero_alt: Two desks side by side: on the left, a matte white humanoid robot handles simple tasks with papers; on the right, a person examines an important document with a magnifying glass.

nos.detalhe: Any task from your sheets: a report, contacts, notes, a new client. Or a one-off question.

Three questions: Is it a big plan or a new system? Has the light model failed twice already? Is this a decision that could cost a lot (paying, negotiating, contracts, a major client)? One "yes" means use the top model. Three "no" answers mean keep it light. Reading and adding up invoices isn’t a decision: it’s routine, so keep it light.
Read, summarize, copy between spreadsheets, prepare the weekly report, draft an email, make a small correction to text or a page. This is most of the boring work.

Planning a new system, a problem the light model got wrong twice, deciding something involving money or a contract (paying, negotiating, accepting terms), or a proposal for a major client. Even here, drafts and the gate still apply.

When the task calls for the top model, the agent says: "I suggest the top model because…" and waits. In chat, you switch models using the selector; in the terminal, you run it again with -m or --model. If it recommends the top model too often or not often enough, adjust the rule.

secoes.legenda: When in doubt, start with the light model and have it say so if it gets stuck. Moving up is easy; using the top model for everything is what gets expensive.

secoes.titulo: Which model is which in your tools
secoes.sub: Names change over time. Check your model list.

texto: In ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, the model selector is at the top of the conversation or near the text box. Each option’s description tells you which one is fast and for everyday use, and which one reasons more or is more capable: the first is your light model, the second is your top model. In Claude, Sonnet is for everyday use and Opus is the more capable one.
In a Project, choose the model at the start of the conversation. To move up, open a new conversation in the same Project with the top model.

In Codex, /model shows the list available on your plan. In the 11/04/2026 list: gpt-6-luna (fast and economical, for easier tasks), gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-6.1-sol (the general-purpose one), and gpt-6-astra (for the most demanding work).
In the command, the model goes after -m.
In Claude Code, /model switches the session model, and --model selects one when you launch it: sonnet for routine work, opus for difficult tasks.
The aliases always point to the latest version in each family.
With a subscription, the top model usually uses more of your usage limit and takes longer to respond.
Routine work on the light model keeps your limit free for when you really need the top model.

secoes.sub: In chat, add it to the Project instructions; in the terminal, add it to the end of AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.

blocos.conteudo:
Model rule:
Use the LIGHT model for routine tasks:
- reading dashboards, spreadsheets, and messages; copying data from one place to another
- weekly reports, summaries, and tables
- email drafts and short replies
- small edits to text, a spreadsheet, or a page

Switch to the TOP model when:
- it's a large plan or a new system
- the light model has made the same mistake twice
- you need to DECIDE something involving money or a contract (pay, negotiate, accept terms), or prepare a proposal for a major client
(reading and adding up invoices or bills is routine: keep using the light model)

When a task calls for the top model, tell me in one line: "I suggest the top model because ..." and wait for me to switch models.
If you're unsure, start with the light model and let me know if you get stuck.
Drafts and the gate apply to both.

Use the model rule above. Here’s my task list (lesson 1).
Return one line per task, in this format:
N | task | light or top | reason in a few words

blocos.rot: Terminal (optional) · the same request at two levels
blocos.conteudo:
# routine work on the light model
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-luna -s read-only -o relatorio.md "report: follow AGENTS.md"
claude -p --model sonnet "report: follow CLAUDE.md" > relatorio.md

# difficult work on the top model
codex exec --skip-git-repo-check -m gpt-6-astra -s read-only -o plano.md "build a plan for the new estimating process"
claude -p --model opus "build a plan for the new estimating process" > plano.md

abas.html:
1 | Weekly website report | light | read and summarize
2 | New contacts and drafts | light | routine, with a gate
3 | Invoices and bills to pay | light | read and add; top if the PDF can’t be read
4 | New client checklist | light | fixed steps
5 | Design the new estimating process | top | new system

• Top model for everything "just in case": routine work gets slow and your limit runs out by Wednesday.
  • Light model for the contract: false economy. Expensive decisions go to the top model, and to you.
  • Switching without telling you: without the "because…" line, you can’t tell whether the rule is working.

secoes.sub: Paste the list the agent returned (or your own). The page checks that each line has just one level, light or top. You decide whether the level is right by asking the three questions.
secoes.rot: Paste your classified list here (one numbered line per task):

exercicios.texto: Paste the routing rule into the instructions for your agents’ Projects (or at the end of AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md).
exercicios.pronto: when you ask "which model would you use for the weekly report?", the agent answers light and gives the reason.

exercicios.texto: Use the "classify my tasks" request with the list from lesson 1. Check it with the checker.
exercicios.pronto: The checker responds OK, and every task that DECIDES something involving money or a contract is marked for the top model or "do not delegate"; reading and adding up invoices can stay with the light model.

exercicios.titulo: E3 · Find your light and top models
exercicios.texto: Open the model selector in the tool you use (or /model in the terminal), read each option’s description, and write down the name of the light model (the fast one for everyday use) and the top model (the one that reasons more).
exercicios.pronto: you have both names written down and ran the weekly report on the light model.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: Which of these tasks should go to the top model?
opcoes: Summarize this week’s new contacts in a simple table.
Copy the invoices into the bills spreadsheet.
Design the company's quoting process from scratch.
perguntas.explica: A new process is a big plan: top model. The other three are routine reading, copying, and drafting—the light model's territory.

perguntas.p: The light model made the same calculation error twice in the report. According to the rule:
opcoes: Try five more times with the light model.
Move this task to the top model, with the note "because the light model made the same mistake twice".
Give up on using an agent for reports.
Switch every task for every agent to the top model, just to be safe.
perguntas.explica: Two failures on the same task are one of the triggers to move it up. Move only that task, with the line "because…", and leave the others with the light model.

perguntas.p: Why not use the top model for everything, since it's better?
opcoes: Because the top model can't do simple tasks.
Because the top model doesn't accept the sheet in its instructions.
Because it usually uses more of your subscription limit and takes longer, with no benefit for routine work.
Because the top model only works in the terminal.
perguntas.explica: The top model can do simple tasks, but it takes longer and uses more of your limit. For routine work, the light model delivers the same result; the top model stays free for tasks that need it.

perguntas.p: In chat, how do you send a difficult task to the top model?
opcoes: Write "use the top model" in the middle of the conversation without changing anything.
Open a new conversation in the same Project and choose the top model.
Create another Project, without the sheet, just for that task.
Get a separate API plan for the top model.
perguntas.explica: Choose the model in the selector. A new conversation in the same Project keeps the sheet and rules, now with the model that reasons more. Asking it to "use the top model" without switching doesn’t change the model, and you don’t need a paid API.

itens.texto: Read, summarize, copy, and draft: quickly, using less of your limit.
Big plan, two failures with the light model, decision involving money or a contract.

itens.t: Move it up and say why
itens.texto: "I suggest the top model because…": the agent suggests it, you switch models, then check whether the rule works.
